business_scope.primary_industry_name: Financial Market News Aggregation and Syndication Feed

stage_1.expense_line_item: Name search and homonimia certificate (RUES / Cámara de Comercio)
stage_1.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff table (tarifa RUES) — fixed fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Ley 1258 de 2008) creating the Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada; Articles 5 and 8 (incorporation instrument requirements), Article 9 (capital subscription, minimum 10% paid-in and two-year payment term); Código de Comercio, Book II, Articles 98-125 and 134-163 (merchant registration and joint stock company rules); Law 222 of 1995 (commercial oversight); Decree 1074 of 2015 (trade regulation and registry proceedings).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (Registro Mercantil), operating through the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) and the 'Camara Directa' online portal; coordinated with DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) for NIT issuance.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation instrument) under Article 5 of Law 1258/2008; a public deed (Escritura Pública) is mandatory only when real property is contributed to the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for a Colombian S.A.S.; the founders freely determine authorized, subscribed and paid-in capital. At least 10% of the subscribed capital must be paid in at the time of subscription and the remaining balance within two years, unless the bylaws provide otherwise (Article 9, Law 1258/2008). No escrow account is legally mandated; a sworn statement of the legal representative or a bank certificate of deposit suffices for registry purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [__COMPANY NAME__] S.A.S.

The founding shareholder, acting under Law 1258 of 2008, resolves:

1. Share subscription: The authorized capital of COP [__] is subscribed and paid in accordance with the bylaws; the capital payment declaration is attached.

2. Registered office: The statutory address is fixed at [__], Colombia, where the principal business premises shall operate.

3. Officers: [__NAME__] is appointed Legal Representative and Chief Executive Officer, and [__NAME__] is appointed Deputy Legal Representative and Compliance Officer, each with the powers conferred by the bylaws.

4. Registry and compliance: The Legal Representative is instructed to register the company with the Chamber of Commerce and DIAN, adopt the corporate books, and implement the licensing obligations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name validation and homonymy clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social – Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-availability search against the RUES database to verify that the proposed name '[__COMPANY_NAME__] S.A.S.' is not identical or confusingly similar to a registered entity. Upon approval, download the Certificado de Homonimia (name availability certificate), which is valid for 30 calendar days and must be attached to the incorporation instrument.
required_dossiers: Online name-search request form
Passport or government-issued ID of the requesting shareholder
Proposed company name and corporate object description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected, file a fresh application offering up to three alternative complete names; each fallback name must independently pass the homonymy filter before the certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the private incorporation instrument and bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders and, where required, a Notary Public or the Cámara de Comercio certifying signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución containing the mandatory provisions of Article 5 of Law 1258/2008: corporate name, principal object (financial market news aggregation and syndication API), registered office address, authorized/subscribed/paid-in capital, share classes and voting rights, administration and legal-representative powers, and resolution of corporate disputes. The instrument must be signed by every founding shareholder, with signatures certified by a notary or an authorized Chamber official; no judicial approval is required.
required_dossiers: Full text of the bylaws / incorporation instrument
Certificado de Homonimia (name certificate)
Valid passport or governmental ID of each founding shareholder
Certified Spanish translations of any foreign corporate documents
Proof of authority for corporate shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or a notary identifies statutory inconsistencies, execute a supplementary 'aclaración' minute or amendatory private instrument correcting the observations and re-submit it within the term granted (typically 10 business days).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registration, fee payment and issuance of the Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (Registro Mercantil), in person or via the Camara Directa portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed incorporation instrument with the corresponding Cámara de Comercio together with the RUES form. Pay the commercial registration tariff and the registration tax (impuesto de registro, approximately 0.5% of the subscribed capital) at an authorized bank or through the portal. After verification, the Chamber issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal and automatically transmits the pre-assigned NIT data to DIAN.
required_dossiers: Executed private incorporation instrument
Certificado de Homonimia
RUES short/long registration form
Appointment and ID of the legal representative and compliance officer
Bank payment receipt of registration fees and registration tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is qualified with observations, the Chamber grants 10 business days for correction; file a written 'subsanación' with the corrected annexes or appeal the registrar's decision before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio within the administrative-law term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RUT/NIT obtaining, tax classification and electronic invoicing activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (MUISCA online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm and download the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) and NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) using the data transmitted by the Chamber of Commerce. Select the corporate tax classification, the main economic activity ISIC 6391 / NAICS 519110, and the applicable ordinary income regime. Activate the electronic invoicing (factura electrónica) obligation, choose an authorized software provider or the free DIAN application, and obtain the invoice resolution and certification.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
Preassigned NIT and RUT confirmation request
Identification documents of the legal representative
Proof of the registered-office address
Bylaws and corporate purpose description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN issues a formal compliance requirement or detects discrepancies, respond within 15 business days with the requested evidence; request a rectification (rectificación) of the RUT through MUISCA if the assigned activities, contact data, or tax cluster are incorrect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate bank account opening and paid-in capital formalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banking institution (corporate account desk) and legal representative's sworn declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the company's name and deposit the paid-in portion of the subscribed capital. The legal representative must issue a sworn capital-payment declaration confirming that at least 10% of the subscribed capital has been paid in; retain the bank certificate and deposit voucher to support the Chamber registration and future statutory audits. This step also establishes the payment rails for clients (SWIFT wire and Stripe) referenced in the commercial model.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
RUT and NIT
Bylaws and corporate books (book of shareholders and minute book)
Identification and UBO (beneficial ownership) declaration of final shareholders
Bank account application form and compliance questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional beneficial-ownership or source-of-funds documentation, submit the complete UBO structure and a statement of commercial substance; alternatively, obtain the capital certificate from another licensed bank within the two-year statutory capital-payment window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer registration with social security system, ARL and SGSST programme
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ARL (Administradora de Riesgos Laborales), EPS, pension fund administrator and Caja de Compensación Familiar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer in the Unified Social Security Registry and enrol the initial payroll in EPS, pension fund, ARL and Severance Fund. Select the ARL risk class corresponding to an administrative software/newsroom operation (low risk, Class I). Adopt the SGSST (Sistema de Gestión de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo) plan under Resolution 0312/2019, including a workplace risk assessment, emergency-response plan, and initial safety training for staff.
required_dossiers: RUT and Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
Employment agreements and payroll data of initial staff
SGSST occupational health and safety plan
Workplace conditions statement and office lease
ARL affiliation form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ARL or EPS rejects the registration due to inconsistent business activity, submit a correction request with the actual administrative nature of the operation, the office lease, and a functional description of the news-aggregation software platform to justify the low-risk classification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal operating license, land-use and fire-safety clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía Municipal / Secretaría Distrital de Planeación (land-use) and Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Registro Integrado de Desarrollo Empresarial before the mayor's office and obtain: (i) the Certificado de Uso del Suelo confirming that the news-office activity is compatible with the zoning of the registered premises; (ii) the fire-safety inspection certificate (Certificado de Bomberos) after physical inspection of extinguishers, emergency exits, and alarm systems; and (iii) the statement of compliance with Law 232/1995 on operating conditions of commercial establishments.
required_dossiers: RUT and Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
Proof of legal occupation of the premises (lease or title)
Land-use certificate application form
Fire-safety equipment inspection form
Solid-waste management commitment letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the land-use or fire-safety inspection results in denial or conditioning, remedy the noted deficiencies through the municipal administrative procedure, request a reinspection, and where applicable appeal the administrative act within the statutory term to the municipal authority's superior body.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Data protection registry before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) – Registro Nacional de Bases de Datos (RNBD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company's personal-data processing activities (subscriber records, contact lists, and financial-news recipient logs) in the RNBD as required by Law 1581/2012 and Section 3.3.5 of Decree 1074/2015. Appoint a data-protection compliance officer, adopt a privacy policy and personal-data treatment policy, and publish them on the newswire API platform; if the company processes more than a de minimis volume of data, update the registry annually.
required_dossiers: RNBD initial registration form (provided by SIC)
Name and contact details of the data-protection officer
Privacy policy and treatment policy
Data-flow description of the news syndication software
Information security and access-control measures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SIC returns the registration for incompleteness or inconsistencies, resubmit the corrected form within 15 business days; if a sanctioning proceeding is opened for non-registration, regularize the registry and negotiate the sanction settlement procedure established by the SIC's administrative rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Secretaría Distrital de Planeación / Planeación Municipal (land-use and urban development) and Alcaldía Municipal (Registro Integrado de Desarrollo Empresarial and operating license under Law 232/1995).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Funcionamiento / Registro Integrado de Desarrollo Empresarial, together with the Certificado de Uso del Suelo and the Certificado de Bomberos.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) / Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) of the territorial jurisdiction of the registered office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category Exempt / Registration Only – office-based software and financial newswire activity with no significant environmental impact; a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is not required. Only municipal solid-waste registration and take-back obligations for e-waste and obsolete IT equipment apply under Resolution 1512/2010.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary wastewater discharges to the municipal sewer must comply with Resolution 0631/2015 limit values; if emergency diesel generators or auxiliary HVAC units are installed, air emissions must not exceed the limits of Resolution 909/2008; hazardous and e-waste must be handled through authorized recyclers in compliance with Decree 1079/2015 and the extended-producer-responsibility obligations for computers and peripherals.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos fire-safety certificate verifying extinguishers, emergency exits, fire alarms, and evacuation signage; structural and seismic-safety clearance per Reglamento NSR-10 (National Building Code) for the occupied premises; SGSST occupational health and safety programme under Resolution 0312/2019; and, where the office is located in a BOMA-style commercial building, the building administrator's fire and emergency coordination certificate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — portal: https://www.dian.gov.co; transactional and e-filing platform: MUISCA (https://muisca.dian.gov.co); electronic invoicing clearance APIs and RUT registration services are hosted on the DIAN web-services platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the S.A.S., the incorporation deed is filed with the local Cámara de Comercio, which pre-registers the company in the RUT (Registro Único Tributario); DIAN then assigns the definitive NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria), which serves as the single TIN/VAT ID. For a 100% foreign-owned S.A.S., the foreign shareholder must deliver apostilled/notarized corporate resolutions and bylaws, appoint a Colombian legal representative, and the representative must submit the RUT application through the MUISCA portal, designating the entity as (i) IRC taxpayer, (ii) responsable del IVA – Régimen Común, (iii) withholding agent, and (iv) exporter of goods/services. The RUT is then updated with the ISIC 6391 activity code and the export-of-services status before the first zero-rated sale. If the foreign principal does not incorporate locally, it may alternatively register a branch (sucursal de sociedad extranjera) requiring parent-company authorization, local attorney appointment, DIAN and Chamber registration, and a separate NIT. Standard issuance is immediate for pre-validated records and up to five business days where physical documentary review is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the S.A.S. is a Colombian tax-resident corporation taxed on worldwide income at the statutory 35% corporate income tax rate, with dividends paid to foreign shareholders subject to the Colombian dividend withholding framework; Colombia does not recognize pass-through or check-the-box elections. Territorial scope applies only to non-residents: foreign beneficiaries without a Colombian permanent establishment are taxed solely on Colombian-source income. The entity is not eligible for tax-exempt-zone treatment unless specifically located in a designated Zona Franca.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box entity classification exists. Available statutory elections and special regimes include: (i) the Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE) under Law 1943/2018 and Law 2010/2019, electable by an eligible S.A.S. with gross revenues up to 85,000 UVT, consolidating income tax, IVA, and withholding obligations; (ii) the optional fiscal consolidation / special economic-group regime for business groups meeting DIAN qualification thresholds; and (iii) elections relating to amortization, depreciation, and inventory methods under the Tax Statute. Hybrid-mismatch neutralization (Law 1955/2019 and Law 2277/2022) is mandatory and automatic: deductions for payments producing deduction/non-inclusion or double-deduction outcomes are denied to the extent of the mismatch; there is no elective hybrid adjustment, and CFC and transfer-pricing rules further restrict offshore deferral.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax — IVA (Impuesto sobre las Ventas), governed by Tax Statute Articles 420–503 and Decree 1625/2016
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no turnover threshold for a corporation: an S.A.S. providing taxable services (including ISIC 6391 financial newswire syndication) is a responsable del Régimen Común and must register for IVA via the RUT prior to commencing taxable activity, irrespective of revenue volume. The 3,500 UVT annual-income simplification threshold under Article 437 of the Tax Statute is available only to natural persons, never to an S.A.S.; exporters claiming zero-rating must register regardless of volume to access input-VAT refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (factura electrónica de venta) applies to all Régimen Común taxpayers under Resolution 000165 of 2023. Each invoice must be generated as structured XML, carry the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) and a QR code linked to the DIAN verification service, and be transmitted through certified software (software propio, proveedor tecnológico, or DIAN's free facturador) via the official REST/SOAP APIs. Most taxpayers, including digital-content operators, are subject to validación previa: DIAN validates, corrects, or rejects each invoice in near-real time before the document is delivered to the buyer; accepted invoices may be disputed through the electronic rejection/acceptance event workflow. Non-compliance results in denial of input-VAT credits and deductions, per-invoice sanctions, and inclusion in DIAN preferential audit lists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 481 of the Tax Statute and Decree 1625/2016 Article 1.3.7.3, exports are excluded from IVA (0% VAT) with full entitlement to refund of input VAT. Tangible goods qualify upon physical departure from Colombian customs territory under an accepted export declaration. Services, including ISIC 6391 financial newswire and news-aggregation API services, qualify as exports of services only if: (i) the recipient is a natural or legal person without tax residence or domicile in Colombia (and without a Colombian PE); (ii) the service is used or exploited exclusively outside Colombia; and (iii) the consideration is paid from abroad and channeled through the authorized foreign-exchange market, unless a legal exception to exchange channeling applies. For cloud/API-delivered syndicated content, DIAN will examine the place of actual use and exploitation; routing merely through a foreign contracting party while the content is consumed in Colombia defeats zero-rating and exposes the operator to 19% IVA and penalties.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación — DEX) accepted by DIAN/Aduana with MUISCA levante record evidencing the export operation
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) proving physical departure of goods from Colombian customs territory (goods exports only)
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Liquidación de Divisas) issued by the authorized Colombia intermediary evidencing receipt and channeling of foreign currency
Export contract, commercial invoice referencing the 0% VAT treatment, and foreign purchaser's tax-residence/proof-of-legal-existence documentation
DIAN service-export certificate and service-receipt statement confirming exclusive use and exploitation of the service outside Colombia (service exports)
RUT updated with export activity codes and Cámara de Comercio certificate evidencing the exporter's legal existence and representation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN applies documentary and systems-based audits to export refund claims, with pre-refund fiscal review (fiscalización) triggered above defined materiality thresholds; the general assessment period is five years, extended to ten years where forgery or fraudulent evidence is involved. Penal sanctions include: (i) an inexactitud penalty of up to 100% of the tax difference, and up to 200% in qualified/aggravated fraud cases; (ii) mandatory repayment (clawback) of the refund received, plus moratoria interest under Article 634 of the Tax Statute computed from the date of refund receipt; (iii) an additional sanction of up to 100% of the improperly obtained refund; (iv) customs penalties for false commodity/offshore-status declarations; and (v) criminal liability for tax fraud and fraudulent procurement of refunds under Article 434 of the Colombian Criminal Code, carrying imprisonment. Adverse findings also trigger exclusion from the exporter registry, revocation of zero-rating benefits for prior periods, and designation as a high-risk audit taxpayer.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Banco de la República / Central Bank of Colombia), acting jointly with the Unidad Administrativa Especial de Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN), under the foreign-exchange regime of Law 9 of 1991, External Resolution No. 8 of 2000, and Circular Reglamentaria DCIN 83.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a managed convertible exchange system. The Colombian peso is freely convertible at market-determined rates for both current and capital account transactions, but all cross-border foreign-exchange inflows and outflows must be canalized through authorized local intermediaries. Current account operations—including export of software services, newswire subscription revenue, royalties, interest, and trade settlements—require no prior central bank authorization but must be reported via the applicable cambio declaration form (Form 3 for services). Capital account operations, specifically inbound foreign direct investment, must be declared and registered with Banco de la República using the Form 4 foreign-investment declaration and the electronic Foreign Investment Registration system. Registration is a statutory precondition for the later remittance of dividends, repayment of capital, and the free transferability of the registered investment. Profit remittance is lawful after corporate income tax and dividend withholding obligations are settled; there is no general limitation on remittance amounts, but each outward flow is screened by the intermediary bank for tax, AML, and exchange-control compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For exports of services, including news aggregation and software subscription products, the entire foreign-currency proceeds amount must be channeled through the Colombian foreign-exchange market within one year of the invoice date or the contractual service completion milestone. For exports of physical goods, the exporter must settle the export proceeds within four months from the date of the export declaration (DEX). The statutory surrender rule is 100% canalization, not a mandatory conversion ratio: the exporter must bring the foreign currency into Colombia through an authorized intermediary, but may choose to hold it in a foreign-currency local account or convert it to pesos. Registered digital service exporters may apply to Banco de la República for special approval to retain proceeds abroad solely for liquidity and reinvestment, subject to complete electronic reporting to DIAN and the central bank. Late canalization or failure to canalize triggers administrative penalties under External Resolution No. 8 of 2000, including fines and suspension of foreign-exchange rights.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account in COP and USD / capital escrow account for foreign investment registration
Operational current account in COP and USD / paying agent account for newswire subscription collections
Operational account in COP with USD clearing through a correspondent network
Operational and temporary capital escrow account for incoming foreign investment

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-medium viability. Colombian exchange-control rules require a resident Colombian legal entity to route its cross-border treasury flows through banks and financial institutions authorized by Banco de la República. Offshore digital EMI platforms (e.g., Airwallex, Wise, Mercury) do not hold Colombian banking or foreign-exchange intermediary licenses and cannot be used as a primary or sole treasury rail. A narrow ancillary use is tolerable for low-value card payments collected from non-Colombian subscribers via a technology platform such as Stripe, but those proceeds must be automatically or subsequently repatriated to a Colombian account and reported under Form 3. An S.A.S. relying on an offshore EMI for concentration or settlement of export receipts will create an unresolved canalization breach and a persistent AML/KYC red flag at local banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Fully remote opening without any in-person touchpoint is not generally accepted for a newly formed S.A.S. whose directors and legal representative are non-residents. The bank's policy requires the legal representative or an authorized attorney-in-fact to appear physically at a Colombian branch to execute account application documents, provide signature cards, and complete an AML interview. If the legal representative is outside Colombia, a Colombian notarial power of attorney with apostille legalization, together with the passport of the representative and every beneficial owner, is required. Some Tier-1 banks permit a preliminary video-authenticated KYC stage for low-risk entities, but final account activation is conditional on the risk committee's acceptance and often on the physical delivery of original documents. Remote opening becomes materially more difficult when the entity has only foreign shareholders and no Colombian national on the board, as the bank treats that structure as enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: All natural-person shareholders and directors are resident outside Colombia, and no Colombian national appears on the legal-entity board or as a local compliance point of contact.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled Articles of Incorporation (Escritura Pública), Chamber of Commerce certificate (Cámara de Comercio) issued within the last 30 days, certified current share registry, passport copies for all beneficial owners, proof of residential and business address in the foreign jurisdiction, sworn source-of-wealth statement for each shareholder, and an executed power of attorney in favor of a Colombian resident agent with identification proving local presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The declared business activity, ISIC 6391 'news syndication', may be misinterpreted by automated bank filters as a money-service business or financial data processing activity subject to Superintendencia Financiera authorization.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Colombian RUT certificate showing the exact CIIU code 6391; a formal legal opinion from Colombian counsel stating that the company only aggregates and licenses financial news and does not take custody of client funds; the standard subscriber license agreement containing an anti-payment-intermediation clause; FATCA/CRS self-certifications; and the enterprise's operational flow diagram proving the absence of any payment-clearing function.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capitalized injection from a non-Colombian parent may be flagged as unregistered foreign investment or suspected money-laundering structuring if the wire reference does not clearly identify its purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorizing the capital contribution; SWIFT MT103 transfer receipt with TSR reference and explicit beneficiary account; the Form 4 foreign-investment declaration as filed with Banco de la República; investor's bank statements evidencing the lawful origin of funds; and a reconciliation memorandum matching the wire amount to the share capital increase in the S.A.S. equity ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regular foreign-currency receipts from overseas newswire subscribers and data clients may create a wire pattern resembling unlicensed money transmission or trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standard commercial subscription and API license contracts; itemized monthly invoices with API-call and usage metrics; authentic platform logs (server access records, token hits, and content-delivery statistics) proving actual service delivery; legal-entity KYC file and beneficial ownership details for each material client; and an audit trail showing that the company never effects payments for or on behalf of third parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A beneficial owner or senior officer is identified as a politically exposed person (PEP), or is located in a jurisdiction subject to enhanced global sanctions scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed PEP questionnaire for every natural person with 10% or greater ownership or management authority; negative sanctions-screening results (e.g., World-Check, OFAC, EU sanctions list) for all UBOs; board minutes designating the company's AML committee to supervise the account; a written enhanced monitoring protocol involving quarterly transaction review; and a copy of the company's internal anti-money-laundering manual adapted for a Colombian entity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign investor must wire the capital contribution in USD, EUR, or COP through standard SWIFT MT103 using the Colombian bank's correspondent or nostro/vostro account. The payment order must name the S.A.S. as beneficiary, include the Colombian NIT number, and the purpose field must state 'Capital increase - Registration of foreign investment under Form 4'. The receiving bank will generate the corresponding exchange-control declaration, and the company must complete the electronic Form 4 and update the Banco de la República investment register within the statutory filing window. Monetary capital contributions cannot be routed through third-party payment platforms, crypto exchanges, or offshore EMI accounts; a direct regulated banking wire is the only compliant lane. For non-monetary capital contributions, such as software licenses or intellectual property, the contribution must be documented by an independent appraiser's certificate and registered as an in-kind foreign investment with the central bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Routine operational disbursements to foreign data vendors, journalists, technology providers and content platforms are executed as SWIFT MT103/MT202 cover payments through the Colombian bank's correspondent network. Because the business is digital news aggregation rather than physical trade, documentary letters of credit are generally neither required nor practical. If a particular counterparty insists on documentary assurance, the acceptable instrument is a standby letter of credit (SBLC, MT760) issued by a first-class bank, while the underlying cash settlement still occurs by MT103. Domestic payments to Colombian freelancers and software suppliers are cleared through ACH Colombia (ACH-C), the PSE real-time payment system, or local checks. Every outbound foreign-currency payment must be backed by a service contract, invoice, or license agreement, with the applicable Form 3 or Form 4 declaration filed by the intermediary bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (COP/USD and COP/EUR) written by a locally authorized bank, with a documented underlying commercial transaction or service flow

Non-deliverable FX forwards (NDFs) for the same currency pairs, executed via a Colombian bank's offshore branch or an accommodated offshore dealer, provided the hedge is recorded in the local FX declarations
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) covering long-term USD/COP balance-sheet exposures tied to foreign-currency liabilities or contracted revenue streams
Plain-vanilla currency call and put options purchased solely for hedging forecasted receivables and payables, with strict prohibition of speculative or uncovered trading

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a fine equal to the renewal fee, restrictions on obtaining legal certificates, and potential administrative cancellation of the commercial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (UAE – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between April 8 and April 19 of the year following the tax period, depending on the last digit of the NIT, as set by DIAN Resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to 5% of the tax due plus monthly default interest; non-filing may lead to asset freezing and forced winding-up.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Registry Update (Actualización del Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN – Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the ordinary shareholders' meeting (held by March 31), typically by April 30 each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to USD 50,000 per updated period, in addition to restrictions on executing high-value transactions and obtaining tax certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due in August of each year; exact date per DIAN Resolution, generally no later than August 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines ranging from USD 1,000 to USD 30,000 depending on the value of unreported transactions; criminal liability for willful omission.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent statutory audit (Revisor Fiscal) required if total assets exceed 5,000 SMMLV (≈ USD 1.8M) OR gross annual income exceeds 3,000 SMMLV (≈ USD 1.1M), or if the company has more than 200 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS standards adopted under Colombian accounting regulation (Decreto 2420/2015); small entities may apply IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para Pymes).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial owners must be updated annually within one month after the shareholders' meeting approving the annual financial statements; share transfers must be reflected in the shareholder register and the RUBF within 15 business days of the transfer. The confirmation is filed electronically with DIAN.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea de Accionistas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 – 400 per year for registered virtual office or representation services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 – 8,000 (if statutory auditor required; average for a small SAS is approximately USD 5,000)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% for Colombian-resident corporations and S.A.S. entities (Colombian Tax Code Article 240, as amended by Law 2277 of 2022).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for financial news aggregation or newswire services. Preferential deductions include: (i) 25% tax deduction for investments in science, technology and innovation under Article 158-2 E.T.; (ii) accelerated depreciation of fixed productive assets; (iii) no additional branch remittance tax if the Colombian entity is a resident company. Certain free-trade-zone regimes may offer reduced 20% corporate rate but are industry/site specific, not applicable to a non-physical digital service provider.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 210 (Declaración de Renta y Complementario para Personas Jurídicas y Asimiladas) filed electronically through the DIAN 'SIE' (Servicios Informáticos Electrónicos) portal and authenticated via 'Certificado Digital'.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The corporate fiscal year is the calendar year. The annual income tax return must be filed and paid between the 10th business day of April and the 14th business day of May of the following year, depending on the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT. Non-resident entities with Colombian-source income are subject to the same deadline schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Identification Number (NIT) assigned by DIAN to the Colombian S.A.S.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must obtain a NIT for the Colombian entity; if the entity only files withholding declarations, a specific non-resident NIT must be obtained from DIAN.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Primary tax residence address of the corporate entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Colombian registered office address of the S.A.S.; for an entity classified as resident, this is mandatory for tax assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable year being declared, format YYYY.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the calendar year applicable, e.g., 2024. Non-resident branches without a permanent establishment file under a separate regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenues from syndicated financial newswire, API subscription feeds, and digital data licensing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Colombian-source revenue; if the non-resident provides digital services to local users, the S.A.S. is the withholding agent and must present the corresponding return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowed costs and expenditures, including data center hosting, software licenses, bandwidth, staff salaries, and professional fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are only permitted if they meet the causality, probity, and territoriality requirements under Article 107 E.T.; payments abroad may be subject to withholding and require evidence of actual service rendering.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after applying statutory adjustments, carried losses, and allowed exempt items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute based on audited accounts. For non-resident entities, net taxable income derived from Colombian-source activities must be calculated separately from foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 61 (Impuesto de Renta a Tarifa General)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax at 35% applied to the net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The S.A.S. is subject to entity-level tax rate of 35%; no differentiation for foreign ownership, but DTA relief may reduce taxable base attribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, including foreign tax credits under applicable double taxation agreements and VAT rebates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may invoke the DTA if the Colombian S.A.S. proves credibility of foreign tax paid; withholding certificate must be included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 90 (Saldo a Favor o a Pagar)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance due to DIAN or amount to be carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay electronically via bank authorized by DIAN; balance must be zero if all withholding tax was passed through properly.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the tax assessed, increased by 1% per each month or fraction of month of delay, capped at 100% of tax due. Late payment interest: daily moratorium interest (intereses moratorios) at the DIAN rate (approximately 2.5-3% per month in 2024). Minimum fine for omission: 10% of omitted value; for non-presentation: COP 20,000 per day up to COP 1 million. Criminal sanction may apply if non-filing is deemed fraudulent.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding tax on dividends paid from taxed profits to non-resident shareholders; 0% if the beneficial owner is a resident Colombian corporation. Additional 5% applies to dividends paid out of profits that had already benefited from a reduced corporate rate or loss carryforward.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke reduced DTA dividend rate (typically 5% on >=25% shareholding or 15% portfolio under treaties with Canada and Spain): 1. Request the Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority for the beneficial owner. 2. Legalize the TRC by apostille or consular legalization. 3. Submit the TRC and Form 210 shareholder identification to the Colombian paying company. 4. Complete and file the DIAN 'Cedula' and information return for cross-border payments. 5. Retain evidence for 5 years. If the TRC is not supplied, the statutory 10% must be withheld and paid.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on cross-border royalty payments: 20%. Statutory WHT on cross-border interest: 20%. Under Colombian DTAs (e.g., Spain, Canada) royalties may be reduced to 15% and interest to 15% if the beneficial owner is a resident of the treaty state and the payment meets the 'practical economic substance' test. Payments for software use are characterized as royalties and subject to 20% unless reproduction beyond internal use is involved.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File if the taxpayer's gross income or total assets at the end of the fiscal year exceed COP 100,000 UVT. For tax year 2024, 100,000 UVT equals COP 4,706,500,000 (approximately USD 1,175,000). The threshold applies separately to gross income and assets; transactions with related parties must be documented if either benchmark is exceeded.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not maintain a stand-alone Economic Substance Regulations statute like the UAE; however, Articles 260-1 through 260-10 E.T. incorporate the OECD arm's length standard, and the GAAR under Article 108 E.T. disregards transactions lacking business purpose. Additionally, Article 143 E.T. requires legal form to reflect economic substance. For financing and IP-dependent operations, the DIAN conducts a six-factor economic substance review (personnel, assets, risk control, location, contractual substance, and beneficiary ownership). An S.A.S. that is only a paper entity without operational substance in Colombia will have interposed party transactions recharacterized and may be denied treaty relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting syndicated newswire revenues from Form 210, inflating management fees paid to offshore related entities, or reclassifying fee income as exempt LOE or non-taxable currency gains.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty under Article 648 E.T.: 20% to 200% of the omitted tax amount, plus moratorium interest at the DIAN rate. Criminal conviction under Article 111 of Law 1766 of 2015 carries 4 to 8 years' imprisonment and fines up to COP 200,000,000. The penalty is non-deductible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shareholders who sign or direct false returns are solidarily liable under Article 793 E.T. when the company is used as a mere façade. The Colombian tax authority can impose travel bans (impedimento de salida del país) and initiate criminal action for fraud on the public treasury.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a Form 210 without the required Local File/Master File after exceeding the 100,000 UVT threshold; applying an unsupported TNMM margin or disregarding credit effects for related-party newswire distribution agreements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty under Articles 260-9 and 260-10 E.T.: 10% of the value of the related-party transactions, or 5% of the transactions when the documentation is incorrectly presented; taxable income may be upward adjusted based on deemed arm's-length result plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives who certify false TP documentation are subject to criminal liability for submission of false declarations under Article 290 of the Colombian Criminal Code, which carries 4 to 8 years' imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Colombian S.A.S. with no staff or operational activity solely to house contractual rights to syndicated finance news content, then routing profits via dividend or royalty payments to a zero-tax jurisdiction, or claiming DTA withholding relief without actual ownership rights.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DIAN may disregard the entity under Article 108 E.T., deny treaty benefits, impose the 35% corporate tax on the full book revenues, and apply a 100% penalty on the avoided tax. Additionally, if the structure is considered an improper instrument to evade taxes, a criminal charge for tax fraud can be added.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The S.A.S. law (Law 1258 of 2008) permits veil piercing when the entity is used to commit fraud. Shareholders and directors may be personally liable for all unpaid taxes plus penalties; civil restitution and prohibition on serving as directors for up to 10 years apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing Swift-wire or Stripe payments from sanctioned/ OFAC-listed entities, failing to conduct basic customer due diligence on syndicated newswire subscribers, or using layered bank accounts to obscure the origin of subscription revenue from a Colombian S.A.S.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Colombian Law 1121 of 2006 and Law 1766 of 2015, money laundering offences carry fines up to COP 48 billion and imprisonment of 8 to 15 years. If the S.A.S. is used as a conduit to move payments from illicit sources, the corporation itself may be interdicted and its operational licenses revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who fail to implement a Simplified Risk Management System (SRMS) or who approve transactions from shell counterparties face personal criminal liability, asset seizure, and travel bans imposed by the Fiscalía General; they may be barred from commerce for life.
